outlook: Medic relies on his long, accurate strikes and devastating power, while Rodriguez is a crafty, technically sound boxer who prefers close quarters. Both enter this welterweight bout on three-fight win streaks. Medic carries physical advantages and has found success at 170 pounds, whereas Rodriguez is aging and may show signs of decline. The writer picks Medic to win by first round knockout.

Blachowicz relies on fundamental skills, intelligence, and composed well-roundedness to weather adversity and wear down opponents, while the taller Stirling uses sound outside kickboxing, solid takedown defense, and occasional shots to keep foes off balance. This matchup pits an aging veteran showing signs of physical decline against an undefeated, fresher rising contender.

Rakic moves up to heavyweight from light heavyweight to face the durable grappler Tybura. Rakic relies on his reach, long jab, leg kicks, and solid fundamentals to dictate range. Tybura closes the distance to use trips, throws, and grappling to ground opponents. Rakic should be the quicker man and hold a reach advantage in this clash. The writer picks Rakic to win by a lopsided decision.

Todorovic brings power and offensive wrestling, while the towering Valentin offers range and grappling. Both fighters are deeply flawed, not terribly durable, and have struggled in the UFC. Valentin needs a clean takedown to utilize his ground skills, but pulling guard is dangerous against Todorovic. The writer picks Todorovic to walk a tightrope, attack with leg kicks, and secure an upset decision victory.

Cepo is an aggressive striker who pairs a brute force brawler approach with smart wrestling, while the taller Urbina relies on range as a striker. Urbina struggles at mid-range, possesses poor takedown defense, and lacks the strength to keep the burly Cepo away. Cepo should easily neutralize that reach advantage by forcing a close quarters battle, whether he chooses to land short range weapons or drag the fight to the canvas.

Janicic brings a rangy, athletic striking approach and a scrambly ground game, while Gugnon counters as a long muay thai southpaw who also looks to initiate grappling exchanges. Both newcomers arrive with similar physical builds and regional success, creating a closely matched contest. Janicic receives a slight home region crowd edge, and the reporter leans toward him due to his greater overall experience and slight size advantage.

Klein brings blistering speed, a powerful kickboxing arsenal, and underrated offensive wrestling against fellow distance striker Musayev. Both men favor striking scraps on the feet and possess sneaky wrestling capabilities. Klein utilizes fast combinations and relentless forward movement to secure close rounds. Musayev enters after a rousing decision victory, remaining unfazed as a heavy underdog previously.

Elliott relies on midrange boxing, well timed takedowns, and forward pressure to make taller kickboxers uncomfortable. Oliveira counters as a rangy, patient orthodox striker with fast hands, crisp combinations, and above average finishing power. Elliott has a path to frustrate and nullify his opponent early. However, the writer expects Oliveira to rise in class, display clear superiority on the feet over the final two rounds, and win by decision.

Nikolic uses a tall, technical kickboxing attack featuring a fast jab and long kicks, complemented by strong defensive wrestling and grappling instincts. Vologdin is a compact wrestle-boxer who likes to feint and spring into range, though he often gets drawn into wild brawls. Nikolic brings veteran poise and superior fight management skills into the Octagon. The expected path to victory favors Nikolic to win by decision.

Buzukja relies on high-volume boxing and pressure to compensate for slow hands and feet, while facing a physical mismatch against Grad. Buzukja struggles with defensive wrestling and frequently goes to the ground, despite being a capable grappler. His gym switch is unlikely to fix deeper issues with his physicality and mid-career approach. Grad enters as the favorite to secure a victory over the struggling Buzukja.

Miloševic brings a technical striking and strong grappling game featuring effective clinch work and heavy top pressure into her debut. Cowan relies on physical wrestling and strength, but struggles with durability and fight management in the division. Cowan needs a tactical blunder or cardio issues from Milošević to win. The writer expects Milošević to avoid these mistakes and secure a dominant decision victory.

Leka relies on size, punching volume, and surprise ground mobility, while Poppeck brings basic striking combinations, hard kicks, and strong wrestling. Leka enters as the younger, natural heavyweight, but his inconsistent wrestling and questionable defense leave openings. Poppeck presents a stern short notice test in this European debut.

Spasić relies on muay thai pressure, utilizing solid calf kicks and a strong left hand, while Luciano acts as a rangy outside striker who prefers high-volume, low-power exchanges. Their contrasting styles create a fun kickboxing matchup on the feet. Luciano enters with more experience inside the promotion and distinct physical advantages. Despite those factors, the analytical edge points toward Spasić securing a narrow decision victory.
